clue.text: It's exhausted us — we had to relax

indicators.note: relaxing loosens things, so the letters before it are let go of their order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiring activity has drained a group of people, who needed a rest afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash hides that 'us we had to' is one run of nine fodder letters, with 'relax' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone drained of all energy is said to look pale and spent.

clue.text: Jonah could hardly have it, unfortunately

definitions.meaning: a Jonah is someone who brings misfortune, so his fortune could scarcely be any poorer than it is
an interjection of regret, said after reporting something disappointing

explanation.surface: The biblical prophet was denied something, which is a pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase is a rueful aside meaning 'alas', and also describes a fortune poorer than a jinx's.

clue.text: Control an animal

definitions.meaning: to guide or direct the course of a vehicle or ship
a young castrated bull raised for beef

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb meaning to guide a course, and a noun for a bullock.

clue.text: Playing quietly, a par is achieved

indicators.note: letters at play move about freely, so the words after it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer, playing calmly, makes the standard score for the hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' is the anagram signal for 'quietly' and the 'a' after it; the golf picture hides that par here just means the same level.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be on a par with someone is to be level with them.

clue.text: It's all right to bag a bit of fruit? What a gall!

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside a container, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: OK is the usual short way of saying all right
an apple is one piece of fruit

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for cheekily pocketing a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a gall!' reads as a cry about cheek, but a gall is also a growth on a tree. 'to bag' puts A inside OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a round growth caused by wasp larvae on one kind of tree is a plant gall.

clue.text: Little Tom and what he sought down under

definitions.meaning: Little Tommy of the English nursery rhyme, who sings for his supper, has this surname
the boy in the rhyme sang for his supper, and this is the Australian slang word for food

explanation.surface: A small boy went looking for something in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme boy's surname is also Australian slang for the meal he sang for.

clue.text: Cot is made up for one suffering without complaint

indicators.note: to make something up is to put it together afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bed is prepared for an uncomplaining patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' is what you do to a bed, and here it is the anagram signal for 'Cot is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the Greek philosophical school, such a person endures hardship with no fuss.

clue.text: First of leaves dropped by blue flower

indicators.note: the letter is let fall from the word that follows, which loses it

parts.note: to blue money is old British slang for spending it recklessly, which is to splurge

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: A blue-flowered plant sheds its earliest leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' is not a colour but an old slang verb for squandering money. 'dropped by' takes L, the 'First of leaves', out of SPLURGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a plant of the euphorbia family with small greenish blooms.

clue.text: With love a good man overcomes discrimination and banishment

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces that overcome another stand on top of it

parts.note: love is a score of nil in tennis, which looks like the letter O
a saint, abbreviated St, is the crossword's good man
racism is discrimination on grounds of race

explanation.surface: Kindness lets a decent person rise above prejudice and exile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcomes' reads as triumphing over prejudice, but in a down entry it only says the first pieces stand above the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: exclusion from a society or group, from the ancient Athenian vote to exile a citizen.

clue.text: Men in a force? That's about right

definitions.text: Men in a force? That's about right

indicators.note: one piece goes about another, meaning around it

parts.note: cops are officers in a police force

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a body of men counts as a force and is told that is roughly so.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer loosely while 'about' puts R inside COPS; the opening words do duty in both readings.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of troops is a group of men within an armed force.

clue.text: Animal rights include the power to move back

parts.note: one right is R, the abbreviation

indicators.note: the pieces before it hold the piece after it inside them

parts.note: the other right is OK, as in all right

indicators.note: the word is to be written in the backward direction

parts.note: a cube is the third power of a number

explanation.surface: Campaigners say that creatures' entitlements cover being free to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal rights' reads as one phrase, but the definition is the first word alone and the plural 'rights' is two different abbreviations. 'to move back' gives EBUC, which 'include' places within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a male deer of a small European species.

clue.text: Meet in the bar

definitions.meaning: to meet an attack or argument is to answer it with an opposing move
the long surface in a pub across which drinks are served

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb for answering a blow or argument, and the serving surface in a pub.

clue.text: See sailors (English) about to enlist

indicators.note: turned about, so the whole run of pieces is read from its far end

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or see
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's sailors

explanation.surface: Someone visits English seamen just before signing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to enlist' reads as 'on the point of joining', but 'about' turns everything before it around; the brackets are only surface decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to sign up as a member, for a course or for military service.

clue.text: This reflects a landing-stage and a schooner, perhaps

parts.note: a pier is a platform built out over water where boats land
a schooner is a tall glass for sherry or beer, as well as a ship

explanation.surface: Something mirrors a jetty and a sailing ship beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The landing-stage makes 'schooner' look like a ship; it is the drinking vessel, a large sherry or beer glass.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tall mirror made to hang on the wall between two windows.

clue.text: Articles abroad about the place to see badgers in disorder

definitions.note: read as a verb: to disturb or throw into confusion

indicators.note: the two pieces before it go about, meaning around, the piece after it

parts.note: un is the French for a, an article in a foreign language
le is the French for the, another foreign article
a sett is a badger's burrow

explanation.surface: Foreign newspaper pieces describe a wildlife site where the animals are in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' is a verb here, not the noun the surface suggests, and 'about' is a container signal rather than 'concerning'. 'Articles' are grammatical ones, French for 'a' and 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to disturb someone's calm or upset an arrangement.

clue.text: What do you do with a futon? Give the matter extended consideration

definitions.text: What do you do with a futon?
definitions.meaning: a futon is a Japanese mattress, and the plain use of one is to lie down and slumber upon it
the idiom for putting off a decision until the next morning

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: delaying a decision overnight is, taken literally, what one does lying on a mattress.

clue.text: Left a child enervated

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: Somebody walked out, leaving a youngster drained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb of abandonment but is only the abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking strength or firmness, floppy and weak.

clue.text: Correspondent invests a day in writing the conclusion

indicators.note: to invest something is to put it into something else, so the day is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: to pen something is to write it, so penning is writing
the end of something is its conclusion
Fri is the short form of Friday

explanation.surface: A journalist spends a whole day drafting the final paragraph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondent' suggests a reporter, but it is someone who exchanges letters. 'invests' is no money matter: it tucks the day between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person exchanges letters regularly with someone, often abroad and never met.

clue.text: The top fifty accommodated in a boat

indicators.note: the number is given room inside the word that follows

parts.note: a pinnace is a small boat carried by a larger ship
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: The fifty highest-ranked people are all housed on one vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The top fifty' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops after 'top'; 'accommodated in' puts L inside PINNACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the highest point or peak, of a mountain or of a career.

clue.text: He promoted a line of footwear

definitions.text: He promoted a line of footwear

parts.words: He promoted a line of footwear
parts.note: reads as a shoe salesman, but points to the Victorian MP who campaigned for the load line painted on ships' hulls, whose name is also a British canvas sports shoe

explanation.surface: A man marketed a range of shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is the safe-loading mark on a ship's hull, named after the MP who fought for it; the same name is a British rubber-soled canvas shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel, a Victorian politician, gave his name both to a ship's load mark and to a gym shoe.

clue.text: Take a quick look round the castle here

indicators.note: turned round, so the word is read from its far end

parts.note: to peek is to glance quickly

explanation.surface: A tourist is invited to have a brief wander about a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like part of a tour of the castle but it turns PEEK the other way; 'here' just points at the result.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the central tower and strongest part of a medieval fortress.

clue.text: One who shoots film near riot

indicators.note: a riot is wild disorder, so the letters beside it are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cameraman records footage close to a violent disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoots film' reads as one phrase, but the definition ends at 'shoots'; 'riot' is the anagram signal for 'film near'.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier armed with a long gun fires it for a living.

clue.text: Projectile starts to turn round, and can easily return

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A missile begins to curve and may well come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' covers all six words that follow, comma notwithstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bullet or shell that leaves a visible trail to show its path.

clue.text: Tax Jenny?

definitions.meaning: to tax is to fix the amount due from someone, to rate or evaluate
a jenny is a female donkey, whimsically a donkey with the feminine ending of lioness or tigress

explanation.definitionFit: To rate for taxation; whimsically, also a female donkey formed like lioness.

clue.text: This is about the centre of haute couture, and about fine clothes

parts.note: ca is short for circa, Latin for about
Paris is the capital of high fashion
on can mean concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A piece of writing covers the heart of the high-fashion world and its elegant outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'about's give different pieces, CA and ON; 'the centre of' is not a middle-letters instruction but describes Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a horse's ornamental covering, and by extension rich dress or finery.

clue.text: Chalice I would give god

parts.note: a chalice is a ceremonial cup
I would contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A worshipper would offer a sacred goblet to a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: he is the Roman deity of love.

clue.text: The skinflint whom I serve houses me

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside, so these words contain the run of letters

explanation.surface: A servant says their stingy employer at least gives them a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' says the words 'whom I serve' hold the run of letters; 'me' is the answer speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mean person who hoards money and hates spending it.

clue.text: Composer of note leading the country

indicators.note: the note comes first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: so is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt soh
the USA is a country

explanation.surface: A distinguished writer of music is at the head of his nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of note' reads as 'distinguished', but 'note' alone is the sol-fa SO, and 'leading' places it first.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip, the American march king, wrote The Stars and Stripes Forever.

clue.text: Father may set about a man in style

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: set the other way about, so the word is read from its far end

parts.note: can and may both express permission
he is the pronoun for a male person

explanation.surface: Dad might attack a fellow, and do it with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' reads as 'attack' but turns CAN (from 'may') into NAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: flamboyant confidence of manner, flair or dash.

clue.text: Seal appears mostly near a river

indicators.note: most of the word is used, so its final letter is left off

parts.note: close means near
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A marine mammal is usually seen close to a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' is not the animal but a fastening. 'mostly' cuts the E from CLOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a cap or fastening that shuts a container.

clue.text: Put off the opening of theatre in 9

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word that follows

parts.note: the animal answering clue 9 across is a kind of deer

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A new playhouse's first night is postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' sends you to the animal at 9 across, used here by its general kind; 'in' puts T, 'the opening of theatre', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to discourage someone from doing something.

clue.text: Handcuff the musicians?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, a metal ring locked round the wrist
a Caribbean group playing tuned oil drums

explanation.definitionFit: A group of Caribbean drum players; read literally, a metal ring such as a shackle.
